title: Implement Dynamic File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) Feature
description: The PulseConnect Sentinel system currently monitors performance metrics and aggregates logs. A key security requirement has been identified: the need to monitor critical system files for unauthorized changes. This task involves implementing a new File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) feature. This feature will require extending multiple services, from the agent collecting data to the alerting service that flags malicious activity. The configuration of which files to monitor must be dynamic, controllable via the existing command infrastructure without restarting the agent.

project_spec.name: PulseConnect Sentinel
project_spec.description:
PulseConnect Sentinel is a socially-oriented system-monitoring suite that treats every server, container and IoT edge device as a "participant" in a community. Instead of silent, isolated infrastructure, each node actively "posts" its health status, performance metrics and security observations to a shared event timeline resembling a social feed. Administrators, automated bots and even other services can follow, react to and comment on these posts, creating a collaborative, conversational approach to infrastructure health.

Built as a constellation of microservices, PulseConnect Sentinel leverages an event-driven backbone where health updates, security-scan findings and configuration changes are published as immutable events. A chain-of-responsibility pipeline enriches each event with contextual data (dependency maps, user-tagged priority, compliance labels) before observers—such as the Alerting Service or the Risk-Score Aggregator—process them. Command Pattern endpoints let operators issue real-time remediation commands (e.g., "restart service", "apply hot-patch") which are validated, logged and dispatched to the relevant node. The overall experience feels like moderating a vibrant social network whose members happen to be services, VMs and network devices.

By framing monitoring as social interaction, the project enables crowd-sourced troubleshooting, transparency and gamified uptime goals, making routine operations more engaging while maintaining rigorous security and performance oversight.
dependencies: cJSON (lightweight JSON serialization for event payloads)
jansson or YAJL (JSON parsing for configuration management)
libinotify (Linux FS change observer for config drift detection)
